::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

The rational benchmark is useful only when students can diagnose where real judgment departs from it. This part moves from adaptive shortcuts to statistical correction and then to context effects.
:::

## Guiding questions

- When do heuristics fit the environment?
- Why do stories overpower base rates?
- How do anchors, frames, primes, and fluency change judgment?

## Chapters

- **Chapter 9:** [Heuristics: The Adaptive Toolbox](../chapters/09-heuristics-the-adaptive-toolbox.qmd) — Simple rules for a world that does not permit complete calculation — About 15 min
- **Chapter 10:** [Feeling and Availability as Shortcuts](../chapters/10-feeling-and-availability-as-shortcuts.qmd) — When emotion and memory answer questions about risk, value, and frequency — About 9 min
- **Chapter 11:** [Resemblance Is Not Probability](../chapters/11-resemblance-is-not-probability.qmd) — Prototypes, stereotypes, conjunctions, and the seduction of a good story — About 10 min
- **Chapter 12:** [Base Rates, Randomness, and Calibration](../chapters/12-base-rates-randomness-and-calibration.qmd) — Statistical intuition begins where the story meets the denominator — About 15 min
- **Chapter 13:** [Biases That Protect a Story](../chapters/13-biases-that-protect-a-story.qmd) — Confirmation, self-serving judgment, and the feeling of knowing — About 13 min
- **Chapter 14:** [Anchors, Halos, Decoys, and Escalation](../chapters/14-anchors-halos-decoys-and-escalation.qmd) — How initial values, global impressions, comparison sets, and prior investment bend judgment — About 14 min
- **Chapter 15:** [Frames Change the Decision](../chapters/15-frames-change-the-decision.qmd) — Facts arrive with attention, meaning, reference points, and implied causality — About 18 min
- **Chapter 16:** [Priming and the Active Mental Context](../chapters/16-priming-and-the-active-mental-context.qmd) — What is already activated changes what the next event means — About 22 min
- **Chapter 17:** [Fluency, Familiarity, and the Feeling of Truth](../chapters/17-fluency-familiarity-and-the-feeling-of-truth.qmd) — Why an easy idea can feel safer, better, and more accurate than it is — About 20 min

## Bridge to the next part

Part III follows the decision beyond choice: how the mind explains what happened and how repeated loops become habits.
